text: Gandharva School of Music
Teacher Collaboration Policy
Effective date: 26 November 2026 | Version: 1.0 | Applies to: all teachers/instructors engaged for the 1:1 online music programme
1. Purpose and Scope

1.1 This Policy explains how Gandharva School of Music ("the School") works with its teachers ("you", "the Teacher") and how our collaboration is structured. It covers trial classes, scheduling, payments, conduct, student safety, privacy, quality and the end of the collaboration.
1.2 The School runs a 1:1 live online music programme. All teaching under this Policy is online and one-to-one, using the School's approved platforms.
1.3 Our aim is a long-term, mutually beneficial association with teachers who are committed to quality music education and to helping students continue their learning journey.

1.4 By accepting this Policy (by signing, ticking an online box, or taking your first class), you agree to follow it. The School may update it from time to time and will inform you in writing. Continuing to teach after the stated date means you accept the update.
2. Nature of the Collaboration

2.1 You are engaged as an independent teaching professional on a contract-for-services basis. You are not an employee of the School, and nothing in this Policy creates employment, partnership or agency. You are not entitled to employee benefits such as provident fund, gratuity, paid leave or bonus.
2.2 The collaboration is non-exclusive, unless a separate written agreement says otherwise. You may teach elsewhere, subject to Sections 11 and 12 (confidentiality and student protection).
2.3 The School does not guarantee a minimum number of students, trial assignments, classes or income. Assignments depend on student demand, your subject and level, availability, and quality.
2.4 You may be engaged for one or more subjects such as [Hindustani vocal / Carnatic vocal / harmonium / tabla / guitar / keyboard / other], as agreed with the School.
3. Onboarding and Teacher Profile

3.1 Before your first assignment you must provide: full name, contact details, qualifications and experience, a recent photograph, ID proof (Aadhaar/PAN or equivalent), and bank details through your Gandharva faculty portal.
3.2 The School may carry out an audition/demo, reference check and background check. A teacher who will teach minors may be asked for a police verification or a self-declaration.
3.3 You must keep your portal profile accurate and up to date (availability, subjects, contact and bank details). You are responsible for losses arising from incorrect details you provided.
3.4 Your portal login is personal. Do not share it. Report any suspected misuse at once.
3.5 The School may use your name, qualifications and photo in its website, brochures and student communication to describe your teaching profile, only with your consent given at onboarding.
4. Free Trial Classes
4.1 Purpose. A trial class is a free introductory session for an interested student so that the student can experience the teaching and the School can recommend the right course.
4.2 Duration. Each trial class is 30 minutes.
4.3 Unpaid. Trial classes are unpaid. You will not receive payment for a trial class, whether or not the student enrolls.
4.4 Number of trials. You may take as many trial classes as you are comfortable with. You may also tell the School when you are not available for new trials.

4.5 Preparation and conduct. For each trial, you should: join on time; briefly assess the student's level, voice or instrument and goals; teach a short, useful exercise or song so the student can see value; explain the learning path and course options in general terms; and avoid making promises about results, exam marks or fees.

4.6 Fees and pricing. Course fees, packages and discounts are communicated by the School's team. You must not quote, negotiate or collect fees from a student or parent, and must not offer your own discounts. Refer all fee questions to the School team.

4.7 After the trial. Submit the trial feedback form on the portal within 8 hours, covering the student's level, strengths, areas to improve, and recommended course. Do not contact the student separately to push enrolment outside the School's process.

4.8 No-show and rescheduling. If a student does not attend, wait for 10 minutes and mark the trial as a Not-Attended on the portal. A trial that you miss or cancel must be informed to the School at least 4 hours in advance so that it can be rescheduled.

4.9 Becoming the regular teacher. Once a student enrolls in a course, you will be assigned as that student's regular course instructor, subject to your subject, level, availability and the student's slot. If a different arrangement is needed (for example, an unavailable slot), the School will discuss it with you.
5. Class Schedule and Delivery
5.1 Frequency. Students generally have 1 or 2 classes per week, depending on the course package they choose.

5.2 Mode. All classes are online. Timings are coordinated between the School, the student and you, based on your availability and the student's. The School will try to respect your availability, but a booked slot, once agreed, is a commitment.
5.3 Class duration. Each class lasts 30  / 60 minutes, as per the student's package.
5.4 Availability. Keep your weekly availability current on the portal. Changes to a standing availability need at least 7 days' notice, so that existing students are not affected.
5.5 Punctuality. Join the class at least 2 minutes early. Start and end on time. A class should be taught for the full scheduled duration.

5.6 Absence and rescheduling by you. Inform the School at least 12 hours before a class you cannot take, except in a genuine emergency (in which case inform as soon as possible). The School will arrange a replacement class or a substitute teacher. A teacher-cancelled class is not paid unless a replacement class is then actually conducted by you.
5.7 Repeated absences. Frequent last-minute cancellations (more than 2 in a month) or no-shows may lead to reduced assignments or end of collaboration.
5.8 Student absence. If a student does not join, wait for 10 minutes, then mark it on the portal as a Not-Attended.
5.9 Holidays. You are expected to follow the School's holiday calendar. Planned leave longer than 7 days must be informed at least 15 days in advance.
6. Class Standards and Teaching Quality
6.1 Teach according to the student's course plan and level. Share practice tasks, notation, references or recordings as needed from the portal itself.
6.2 Maintain a clean, quiet, well-lit setting with a stable internet connection, a working camera and good microphone, and headphones if needed. Keep your camera on during classes.
6.3 Use the School's approved platform and accounts only.
6.4 After every class, record on the portal: attendance, topic covered, homework assigned and short progress notes, within 24 hours. Payment is based on these records.
6.5 Give each student a short progress report every 3 months or on completion of a level, as per School format.
6.6 Be patient, respectful and encouraging. Adapt your teaching to the student's age, ability and goals. Avoid comparisons, ridicule or harsh criticism.
6.7 The School record classes for quality, training and safety purposes, and may collect student feedback. Feedback and ratings are used to improve teaching and in decisions about assignments.
6.8 You must stay within the course plan and the School's curriculum guidelines and must not promote any other teaching service, course, event or product during class.
7. Payment Structure

7.1 Rates. Your payment rate depends on the time slot and your teaching experience. Rates are discussed with the School's team in person and recorded in your faculty account, which forms part of this Policy.
7.2 Changes in rates. Rates may be revised by mutual discussion. A revised rate applies only for the new upcoming student from the date confirmed in writing, and not to existing students.

7.3 Paid sessions. Only completed paid sessions are payable. The following are not payable: free trial classes; classes you cancel or miss without a replacement being conducted; classes not recorded on the portal; classes that could not take place because of your technical failure or late joining, or classes cut short by you.

7.4 Classes affected by the School's side. If a class cannot be held because of a failure on the School's side, or if the student cancels late (as per the School's student policy), the School will decide how it is treated for payment and will tell you.
7.5 Special cases. Make-up classes, workshops, recitals, demo classes for groups, content creation and exam preparation sessions, if any, will be paid only as agreed in advance in writing.
8. Payment Cycle and Payment Method
8.1 Weekly cycle. Payments are processed every Monday for the classes conducted in the previous week. The week runs from Monday 00:00 to Sunday 23:59 IST.
8.2 Basis. Payment is calculated on the completed paid sessions recorded on the portal and verified by the School. The School may check attendance records, class logs and recordings before paying.

8.3 Payment account. Payment is made only to the bank account details that you have provided on your Gandharva faculty portal. The School will not pay to any other account, wallet or person. To change your account, update it on the portal and inform the School at least 7 days before the change is to take effect. A change may need re-verification.

8.4 Payment statement. A weekly statement showing the sessions counted, rate and amount will be available on the portal. Raise any discrepancy within 7 days of the statement. After this period, the statement is treated as accepted, except for clear errors.
8.5 Delay. If a Monday is a bank holiday or a technical delay occurs, payment will be made on the next working day. The School will inform you of any longer delay.
8.6 Adjustments. If a payment was made in excess or by mistake, or for a class later found not to have been conducted, the School may adjust the amount against future payments or ask for a refund.
8.7 Disputed sessions. Sessions under review (for example a student complaint or missing record) may be held back until the review is complete. Undisputed amounts will be paid.

8.8 Taxes. Payments are subject to applicable tax deductions (such as TDS), as required by law. The School will provide a certificate where applicable. You are responsible for your own tax returns, GST registration (if applicable) and other tax matters.
8.9 No payment on termination for serious misconduct. On termination for serious misconduct (Section 14), the School may withhold payment for sessions affected by the misconduct, subject to law.
9. Trial-to-Enrolment Conversion
9.1 You are welcome to conduct multiple trial sessions to connect with prospective students.
9.2 The School monitors the conversion of trial students into paid-course enrolments for each teacher, together with student feedback and trial quality.

9.3 If your conversion rate remains low over 6 trials, the School may reduce the number of trial assignments allocated to you or temporarily stop assigning further trials. This is a business and quality decision, and does not affect payment for paid classes already taken.
9.4 Before such a step, the School will, where practicable, share the numbers with you and offer feedback, coaching or a review of a sample trial, so that you have a chance to improve.
9.5 The School may restore trial assignments when quality or conversion improves, or on mutual discussion.

9.6 Conversion depends on many factors, including student interest, budget, schedule and the School's follow-up. The School will consider these factors fairly and will not judge you only on one number.
9.7 You must not influence conversion by unfair means, such as giving false promises, offering private discounts, or encouraging a student to join outside the School.
10. Student Privacy and Personal Details

10.1 Your personal details stay private. You must not share your personal contact details (personal phone number, WhatsApp number, email, social-media accounts, home address, bank details or any similar private information) with students or parents, and must not ask for or accept theirs.

10.2 All communication through the School. All communication with students and parents must be through the School's approved channels and platform. If a student or parent asks for your number, politely say that the School's team will help and inform the team.

10.3 Student details stay private too. You may see a student's name, age, level, schedule and limited contact details, solely to teach. You must not copy, store, share, post or use student data for any other purpose, and must not contact a student outside the School's channels.

10.4 No private classes. Do not offer, accept or agree to private classes, payments or arrangements directly with a student or parent. Do not accept gifts of money, and any gift of value must be reported to the School.

10.5 Data protection. You must handle personal data in line with applicable Indian law, including the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, and with the School's instructions. Delete or return any student data in your possession when asked, or when the collaboration ends. Report any data leak or loss to the School immediately.

10.6 Photos and recordings. Do not photograph, screenshot, record or livestream a class, or share any student's image, voice or performance on any platform, without the School's written permission. Recordings made by the School are School property and may be used as per its Privacy Policy.
10.7 Devices and security. Keep your device, accounts and portal login secure, update software, and do not use public or shared devices for classes.
11. Confidentiality

11.1 You must keep confidential all non-public information of the School, including: student and parent data; fee structures and packages; teacher rates; business plans; lead and enrolment data; curriculum, notations and teaching material; internal policies; and portal content.
11.2 You must not copy, share, publish or use such information except for your work with the School.
11.3 This duty continues for 2 years after the collaboration ends, and for student personal data, for as long as you hold it.
11.4 This does not apply to information that is public, that you lawfully knew before, or that you must disclose by law (inform the School first where allowed).
12. Student Protection and Non-Solicitation

12.1 During the collaboration. While you are engaged with the School, and for 6 months after it ends, you must not directly or indirectly solicit, induce or accept any student introduced to you by the School (including trial students) for classes outside the School, or ask them to leave the School.

12.2 If a student independently contacts you after the end of the collaboration, you must tell the School and handle it in good faith. Nothing here prevents you from teaching students you had before joining the School.
12.3 You must not use the School's lead and trial information for marketing your own classes, channels or products.
13. Code of Conduct and Child Safety
13.1 Professional behaviour. Be punctual, courteous and professional. Dress modestly and appropriately, and keep the background neutral and free of distractions.
13.2 Respect. Do not discriminate on the basis of religion, caste, gender, age, disability, region, language, or any other ground. Do not make offensive remarks or jokes.

13.3 Zero tolerance for harassment and abuse. Any form of sexual, verbal, emotional or physical harassment, bullying, exploitation or inappropriate behaviour towards any student, parent or staff member is strictly prohibited and may lead to immediate termination and legal action.

13.4 Minors. For students under 18: do not message, call or video chat with the student privately outside scheduled classes or the School's channels; do not ask for personal photos or details; do not discuss personal, romantic or inappropriate topics; do not meet in person; and keep communication about the student's progress with the parent/guardian through the School. If a minor is alone, remain strictly professional. Where possible, a parent may be present or nearby during the class.

13.5 Reporting. If you see or suspect harm to a student, or if a student shares something concerning, report it to the School's designated officer at once. The School will take it forward as per law, including the POCSO Act, 2012, where applicable. Do not investigate yourself or promise secrecy to a child.
13.6 Substances. Do not attend classes under the influence of alcohol or drugs.
13.7 Social media. Do not post about students or about the School in a way that could harm students, the School or its reputation. Do not make public comments on School matters, fees or students.
13.8 Conflict of interest. Disclose any relationship with a student or parent that could affect your impartiality.
14. Suspension and Termination

14.1 By you. You may end the collaboration by giving 30 days' written notice. During the notice period you must continue to take classes and help hand over students smoothly. If you leave without notice, the School may withhold the payment for the last pay cycle to the extent of any loss caused, subject to law.

14.2 By the School, with notice. The School may end the collaboration by giving 15 days' written notice, for example where there is a lack of students in your subject, repeated quality concerns, repeated absence, or a business change.

14.3 Immediate action. The School may suspend or end the collaboration immediately where: you are found to have harassed, abused or endangered a student; you shared your personal details or took students outside the School; you breached confidentiality or data privacy; you gave false information or documents; you took part in fraud; you were convicted of or credibly accused of a serious offence; you caused serious harm to the School's reputation; or you repeatedly breached this Policy after a warning.
14.4 Process. Except where immediate action is needed for safety, the School will tell you the concern and allow you to respond before final action. You may appeal to the Director within 7 days.

14.5 Handover. On ending, you must stop using School accounts, return or delete School material and student data, and complete a handover of student progress notes. Pending undisputed dues will be paid in the next payment cycle (Section 8.1).
14.6 Student transition. The School alone decides how students are reassigned to another teacher. You must not influence students about the change.
15. Intellectual Property

15.1 School material. Curriculum, notations, lesson plans, videos, recordings, templates and branding created or provided by the School belong to the School. You may use them only to teach School students.

15.2 Your material. You retain ownership of the compositions and teaching material you created independently and before joining. If you create material specifically for the School at its request or on its payment (for example recorded lessons, notations, courses), the School may use it without further charge, and the rights will be as agreed in writing.
15.3 Third-party content. Do not use pirated or unlicensed material in classes. You are responsible for the copyright compliance of any material you introduce.
15.4 Brand. You may say that you teach with the School. You must not use the School's name or logo for any other purpose, or imply that your own classes are those of the School.
16. Communication, Grievances and Feedback
16.1 Official communication is through the portal, email, WhatsApp or phone of the School's team. Keep your contact details updated and reply within 24 hours on working days.
16.2 Support contact: Aman Kumar, Phone/WhatsApp : +918092621301 , 9:00-21:00 IST.

16.3 You may raise concerns about payments, scheduling, students or conduct with the School's team. Concerns about harassment or safety may be sent directly to the Director. These will be handled confidentially and without retaliation.
16.4 The School will acknowledge your concern within 3 working days and aim to resolve it within 15 working days.
16.5 Teachers are invited to share suggestions for the programme and curriculum.
17. Limitation of Liability
17.1 The School is not liable for a Teacher's loss of income due to a lack of students, student cancellations, platform failure, holidays or events beyond its control.
17.2 You are responsible for your own equipment, internet, power and device. The School is not responsible for any harm or loss to them.
17.3 You are responsible for loss caused to the School or a student by your negligence, misconduct or breach of this Policy, to the extent allowed by law.
17.4 Nothing here limits liability that cannot be limited by law.
18. Governing Law and Disputes
18.1 This Policy is governed by the laws of India.
18.2 The parties will first try to resolve disputes through discussion with the School's management.

18.3 If not resolved, the courts at [City, State] will have exclusive jurisdiction. [Optional: disputes may be referred to arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, with a sole arbitrator appointed by the School and the Teacher jointly, seat at [City], in English.]
19. General
19.1 Entire understanding. This Policy, your confirmation message/email (with rates) and any written agreement signed by you make the whole understanding between you and the School.
19.2 Severability. If a clause is held invalid, the rest remains valid.
19.3 No waiver. If the School does not enforce a clause at any time, it may do so later.
19.4 Assignment. You may not transfer or sub-contract your classes to another person without the School's written approval.
19.5 Electronic acceptance. Acceptance by ticking an online box, email, or digital signature is binding.
19.6 Language. This Policy is in English. A Hindi version is available on request, and English prevails if there is a conflict.
